items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Mercer was -- you know, me and my wife, we practically raised Mercer.

ctx.x: Mercer says -- let me see, Mercer says it was done by a jealous woman.

No, it wasn't done by no jealous woman. Who done it, I don't recall now. No jealous woman did that to him. No way. And Mercer, Mercer was -- you know, me and my wife, we practically raised Mercer. Mercer was a kid. He don't -- I don't care what he wrote, he wasn't big enough to dig something like that. And I've never read his book but he lost a lot of friends when he wrote that book. I never heard it. Everybody in our club, Duke Ellington Jazz Society, put him down. I'd put him down, and my being like a father to…
was around our band that much. How can he write about our band, because he wasn't around us. No, he wasn't. He was off somewhere, in Juilliard School somewhere. He never was around there.
